releases.title: Public MVP
releases.goal: Hikma AI ships as a neutral open-source CLI: brew on macOS and Linux, an install script elsewhere, and skills from any repo.
releases.exit: A public repo with a tagged release installs via brew and the install script, installs and pushes skills against a real registry, and contains no bundled registry.

releases.title: Registry workflow
releases.goal: Make the registry workflow solid: restore from the lockfile, coexist with gh skill, and validate registries in CI.
releases.exit: hikma sync restores a repo from the lockfile, skills installed by gh skill are adopted cleanly, custom agent layouts work, and a GitHub Action validates registry pull requests.

releases.title: Trust
releases.goal: Make installs verifiable and releases signed.
releases.exit: Frozen installs from the lockfile, skill verification, and signed release artifacts are available.

releases.title: Stable
releases.goal: Stable contracts, hardened quality, and complete docs.
releases.exit: Config keys, the lockfile format, and the skill layout are documented and versioned; CI covers all supported platforms end to end.

releases.title: Parked
releases.goal: Ideas that gh skill already covers or that wait for demand.

phases.title: Foundation and Rebrand
phases.goal: Create a Claude-only planning repo and define the safe migration path into Hikma AI.
phases.exit: The repo has agentkan planning, Claude instructions, and a reviewed migration checklist with no organization references.

epics.title: Claude-only project foundation
epics.goal: Set up the repo so Claude can operate from one board and one instruction file.
epics.exit: CLAUDE.md, docs/board, and the local agentkan Claude skill exist and validate.

Install the agentkan skill for Claude
Validate the board schema

epics.title: Public identity and naming
epics.goal: Lock the public identity around Hikma AI and the hikma CLI.
epics.exit: README, command examples, package names, and release text consistently use Hikma AI and hikma.

tasks.title: Confirm project name, CLI name, and repository slug
Write neutral positioning and tagline

epics.title: Source import audit
epics.goal: Identify exactly what can be copied, renamed, generalized, rewritten, or omitted for the public CLI-only tool.
epics.exit: A migration checklist exists for code, templates, docs, workflows, package metadata, and the removal of bundled registry behavior.

tasks.title: Inventory commands, packages, templates, tests, and release files
List private defaults and organization-specific references to remove
Identify bundled registry files and behaviors to omit
Decide import strategy: history copy, clean copy, or rewrite

phases.title: CLI With External Registries
phases.goal: Make the CLI usable by any internet user with their own separate registry repository.
phases.exit: A user can initialize Hikma AI, point it at a separate registry such as hasankhatib/ai, and install or update skills without private assumptions or bundled registry content.

epics.title: User-owned registry configuration
epics.goal: Replace fixed registry assumptions with explicit user-owned registry configuration.
epics.exit: The CLI can read, set, validate, and use a registry URL from project or user config, including github.com/hasankhatib/ai.

epics.title: Neutral scaffold templates
epics.goal: Ship templates that work for general open-source and private projects.
epics.exit: Generated files mention only the user's project, selected agent, and configured registry.

epics.goal: Make skill list, install, create, update, and publish flows work with external registries.
epics.exit: Skill lifecycle commands are documented, tested, and independent of any fixed registry owner or in-repo skills folder.
